text:
**For a full recharge in one day, plan on about 250-350 W of panels in good sun. If you can wait a day and a half, a 200 W panel is enough.**

**The formula**
Panel watts ≈ 1,000 Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75). The 0.7-0.75 factor covers heat, panel angle and charging losses, since panels rarely deliver their rated watts ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).

**Panel size needed to refill from empty in one day**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts |
|---|---|
| 3 | ~450 W |
| 4 | ~340 W |
| 5 | ~270 W |
| 6 | ~230 W |

These come from [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) gives about 300 W for a good summer day, and 700 W or more in a northern winter with about 2 sun hours.

**If you can wait longer**
- A 200 W panel on an average US day (4.5 sun hours, 70% efficiency) gives about 630 Wh per day. That refills a 1,000 Wh station in roughly 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)).
- A 400 W panel does it in under a day.
- A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives about 200 W for a 1,000 Wh station ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Check these before buying**
- **Solar input limit:** Your station caps the watts it accepts. Many 1,000 Wh units take 200-800 W, and panels beyond the cap add nothing.
- **Voltage range:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input window. Wiring panels in series adds voltage and can damage the station.
- **Loads:** If you run devices while charging, your net charging is slower.
- **Season:** Winter and cloudy weather can cut output by half or more.

**One option for a 400 W panel**
The [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) lists at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (checked 2026-10-21). It has a 45.3 V Voc, so it suits 12-60 V inputs but not low-voltage ones such as 12-28 V. It weighs 18.5 kg. The link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission if you buy.
